newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index romps to another record high.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index romps to another record high.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average charged into record ground for the third time this week Thursday as blue-chip stocks celebrated the good news that inflation was still not a threat to the economy.

The Dow index jumped 76.19 points to 6,625.67, beating the last record close of 6,600.66, set on Tuesday. It briefly climbed more than 100 points in late afternoon before backtracking on profit-taking.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,610 to 931 on active volume of 554 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Stocks got an initial boost from the December Producer Price Index, which confirmed that inflation remained in check at the wholesale level.

The report triggered a sharp rebound in the bond market, lifting the benchmark 30-year Treasury more than a full point, lowering its yield 6.75 percent from 6.84 percent on Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.

Overall, wholesale prices rose 0.5 percent in December, the Labour Department reported. While the increase was more than economists had generally forecast, most of the rise was attributable to higher energy prices.
The so-called "core" rate, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, edged up only 0.1 percent, which was in line with analysts' forecasts.
With pressure on interest rates waning, investors held to a path they have repeatedly taken recently and seized the opportunity to buy after Wednesday's 51-point drop in the Dow.
"The conventional wisdom is still to buy on every dip," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer and Co.
The market kept with another recent trend, Metz noted, because most of the buying was focused on large capitalisation stocks.
"In general, the money is coming in through intermediaries like mutual fund managers," he said, "and they are still opting to buy the big names."
Analysts said the flood of cash finding its way to mutual funds added fuel to the market's ascent.

"We're in the midst of the deployment of funds that takes place at the beginning of the year," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "That liquidity is still a powerful driver for this market."

So powerful, analysts said, that investors were apparently able to overcome the caution that generally creeps in ahead of the closely watched monthly employment and wage report. Those figures are due early Friday and many analysts consider them more important than the PPI.

"I've got to say this rally is rather impressive ahead of what is supposed to be an important number," Metz said, adding that among indicators on the economy and inflation, he ranked the employment report "No. 1."

Among the big winners were the shares of oil companies, which benefited from the recent jump in crude oil prices and a bullish comment by a Dean Witter analyst about several oil stocks and the outlook for crude oil prices.
Crude oil for February delivery closed at $26.37 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange, nearing its six-year peak of $26.80 hit in late December.
Exxon Corp. rose 3-1/4 to 102-3/4 and Texaco Inc. climbed three to 105.
Hughes Electronics Corp. rose two points to 63-1/8 on news that Raytheon Corp. and Northrop Grumman Corp. each bid $9 billion or more for Hughes' missile and defence business.
All three companies declined to comment but investment bankers familiar with the situation confirmed the bids.
Raytheon fell 1-1/4 to 47-1/2 and Northrop slipped 1-3/8 to 77-7/8.
Neiman Marcus Group Inc. tumbled 3-3/8 to 23-3/8 after the company said its quarterly earnings would fall short of expectations because of disappointing Christmas holiday sales.

CIDCO Inc. slid 5-3/16 to 12-11/16 after Alex. Brown downgraded the shares. The company, a maker of caller identification telephone equipment, said late Wednesday that it would post an operating loss in its fourth quarter.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 5.85 points to 1,326.20.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.44 to 754.85. The American Stock Exchange index was up 5.02 at 581.74.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.33 to 398.58. The average share was up 35 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,325.944, up 56.303, or 0.77 percent.
